title: When a comment's mechanism claim keeps turning out false at the edges, stop enumerating the edges and assert the outcome property instead
decided_by: Dev + BA + SecOps, ratified during #63's Phase 4 panel (issue #63, merged to main as 012db65, PR #77)
content: Standalone rule, generalising past gate-phase-entry.mjs: when a documentation comment asserts HOW two independent mechanisms relate (a shared definition, a matching parse function, a matching throw order), and successive attempts to state that relationship precisely keep turning out measurably false at some edge, the fix is not a fifth, more careful attempt at the mechanism claim -- it is to stop describing the mechanism and assert only the OUTCOME PROPERTY that holds across every measured case. A mechanism you cannot pin down should be described by what it GUARANTEES, not by WHEN or HOW it fires. Origin: #63 corrected a comment in gate-phase-entry.mjs claiming a relationship between this guard's in-flight predicate and pipeline-status.mjs's 'possibly stuck' filter. Four successive draft corrections were each independently falsified by direct measurement, with the test suite green through every draft (the suite pins that the sentence moved, never what it asserts): (1) 'the guard reuses pipeline-status.mjs's definition' -- false, no shared symbol exists, each module holds its own literal; (2) 'an undatable record is neither stuck there nor in flight here' -- false, pipeline-status.mjs substitutes the file mtime for an absent/null updated_at via `??`, so the two predicates fire together on that case, and diverge only on the narrower case of an unparseable STRING; (3) 'the two date functions agree on ISO strings and diverge elsewhere' -- false, `new Date(string)` delegates to `Date.parse`, so they agree on every string including non-ISO ones, and diverge only on non-string values, and not even all of those (`updated_at: 12345` is classified by one side and never reached by the other, because `--json` mode never calls the function that would classify it); (4) a claim about which of two throw sites fires first with multiple issue dirs -- false, `localeCompare` coerces its argument not its receiver, so the throw depends on readdir position, not dir count. What shipped instead deletes all four mechanism claims and states only: 'pipeline-status.mjs's stuck filter is not reached on any path for a value this guard treats as in-flight-forever' -- true across every case measured, and true independent of which comparator throws, which function parses which way, or which literal either module holds. WHY THIS GENERALISES: a comment enumerating a mechanism's edges is a claim about implementation details of TWO modules that nothing forces to stay in sync; every edge it gets right is luck until the next edit to either module. A comment asserting an outcome property is falsifiable by ONE measurement and, once true, stays true under far more classes of future edit to either module's internals, because it does not depend on HOW either module reaches that outcome. APPLY THIS TEST before writing (or accepting a review round on) any comment that describes a cross-module relationship: can you state what is GUARANTEED without describing HOW either side computes it? If not, the comment is one edge case away from being wrong the same way these four were. See knowledge/living-context/architecture--gate-phase-entry-inflight-boundary.json for the full falsification detail and the shipped wording.
